newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian equities gain in buoyant market.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian equities gain in buoyant market.

text.p: Nigerian equities on Friday made a healthy advance to finish the week in a buoyant fashion that has seen prices soar on improved operating results, traders said.
The all-share index was steady at 7364.24 from 7364.25 on Thursday.
"Trading was boosted by increased volume and Cadbury's full-year result," said one trader.
The food and beverages giant posted after-tax profit of 823 million naira to end-December 1996 from 605.9 million in 1995.
Its stock rose the maximum five percent permitted, closing 1.29 naira higher at 27.09 naira.
"The stock is bound to soar even higher in coming weeks because more investors are likely to want a share in its success," said a trader.
Coca-Cola bottler Nigerian Bottling Company, another advancing food sector stock, closed 50 kobo up at 38.80 naira, while Nestle went 30 kobo higher at 58.80 naira.
Shares of leading banks ended stronger on undiminished demand as did oil marketing companies and conglomerates.
Union Bank was 9.75 naira, up 23 kobo, First Bank was 11.00 naira, 20 kobo up and UBA gained 25 kobo to close at 8.50 naira.
Lever Brothers was 15 kobo stronger at 17.55 naira and UAC added to kobo at 9.70 naira but PZ Industries continued its downtrend, falling 40 kobo to 27.00 naira.
Healthcare firm Smithkline Beecham lost four kobo at 8.00 naira because investors were willing to sell large volumes.

Some 6.2 million shares of shoemaker Bata, which had been unsold from a recent rights offer, were traded on Friday as the usually inactive footwear sector came alive. Bata gained two kobo at 52 kobo while Lennards finished three up at 73 kobo.
Unipetrol was 50 kobo more at 69.40 naira and still retaining its position as the dearest stock.
"Demand is still strong at that price, indicating buyers are prepared to bid higher next week," said one trader.
Mobil and National Oil closed at 57.50 naira and 54.40 naira, respectively, each gaining 40 kobo.
